correctness.rationale: Direct Boolean calculations prove \(F^3=SF\) and \(F^2x=Sx\) iff cyclic 101 is absent. Image=avoiding-101 set implies periodic entrance by t=1 and \(F^2=S\) on that image. For even times reduce to spatial periods \(g=\gcd(n,m/2)\). For odd times \(g=\gcd(n,m)\) odd, derive \(x_i=(1-x_{i-r})(1-x_{i+r})\) and use \(\gcd(r,g)=1\) to equate fixed points with maximal independent sets of one g-cycle. Transfer matrices, Perrin recurrence and Möbius inversion then give formulas. verify_rule3.py exhausts binary states for \(3\le n\le14\), comparing image/shift identity and 204 temporal fixed-point counts; verify_independent.py independently counts pattern avoidance, Perrin cycle conditions and integral orbit populations through \(n=19\). Finite checks corroborate, not prove, unbounded n.

value.rationale: The theorem supplies a complete, all-length and all-time fixed-point/primitive temporal orbit count for a canonical nonlinear cellular automaton, unifying two distinct combinatorial transfer systems: forbidden 101 words and maximal independent sets (Perrin sequence). Exact recurrent/transient census and asymptotic density are natural global dynamical invariants, not an arbitrary finite slice. The general pointwise Rule 3 dynamics and independent-set enumeration are already known, but the full temporal enumerator and odd-time bijection are not listed in inspected sources.
